Mina: Quick heads-up — two private VPC tenants in us-east-2 pushed sustained burst traffic and hit the pool ceiling ~2026-03-15T15:02Z. Gateway started queueing and we returned a small spike of 429s. Creating a short playbook we can hand to SEs and customers.

Rachel: Can you paste a representative log line? want to confirm which headers we exposed and if clients retried aggressively.

Mina: Sample from gateway collector (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T15:02:14.312Z tenant=acct-123 pool=private-us-east-2 model=rw-2b request_type=chat latency_ms=2800 status=429 headers={"x-rw-capacity":"util=93%","x-rw-queue":"len=18"}
```
Most failures were short chats (<60 tokens) but high concurrent QPS from a handful of API keys.

Ben: TL;DR guidance we should recommend to customers: client-side admission + small retry/backoff + cheap-model fallback. Server gives soft signals via x-rw-capacity/x-rw-queue so clients can be adaptive.

Alice: Posting a compact Go leaky-bucket snippet for SDKs — tiny state, very conservative:
```go
// per-key state (in-memory)
const rate = 10 // tokens/sec target
const burst = 20
var allowance = burst
var last = time.Now()
func allowOne() bool {
  now := time.Now()
  dt := now.Sub(last).Seconds()
  last = now
  allowance = math.Min(float64(burst), allowance + rate*dt)
  if allowance < 1 {
    return false
  }
  allowance -= 1
  return true
}
```
Recommend values: start at 10 QPS per API key for private pools, burst up to 20. Lower for constrained pools.

Sasha: Also recommend tokens-based weighting: count short inferences = 1 unit, long generation or high n/beam = 5+ units. That prevents noisy short calls from starving long workers.

Rachel: For retries, suggest capped exponential backoff with full jitter and an upper bound of ~1s for interactive UIs. Example JS snippet:
```js
async function retryWithJitter(fn, attempts=5){
  for(let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn() }
    catch(e){
      if(e.status !== 429) throw e
      const base = Math.min(1000, 40 * (2**i))
      const wait = Math.floor(Math.random() * base)
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait))
    }
  }
  throw new Error('retries_exhausted')
}
// fallback: if persistent 429s, reduce model -> 'rw-1b-quant' or lower max_tokens
```

Mina: On the server-side we suggest exposing a hint header customers can send: X-Client-Hint-Priority: low|normal|high. Note: we treat it as a best-effort hint and will still enforce fairness by API key and tenant.

Ben: Add monitoring/alerts section for customers: watch 429_rate, queue_depth (x-rw-queue), pool_utilization, and 95p latency. Suggested thresholds: 429_rate > 0.5% sustained over 10m -> page ops; queue_depth > 10 -> warn; pool_util > 85% -> scale/review.

Alice: Business guidance to include: if bursts are a regular pattern, recommend Reserved Dedicated burst add-on or increase committed capacity for peak windows. Document the cost tradeoffs: reserved capacity reduces 429 risk but increases committed spend.

Sasha: Also useful: define quick fallback tiers for customers to implement in the SDK: 1) reduce max_tokens by 50% 2) switch to a cheaper quantized model 3) respond with cached summary if available.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled private-pool-us-east-2 by +4 GPUs at 2026-03-15T15:04:05Z :rocket:

Mina: Action items to ship as a one-pager for SEs + a tiny code gist for customers:
- Mina: draft the playbook + example snippets (ETA: today EOD)
- Ben: add 'X-Client-Hint-Priority' proto stub and a note in the API docs (ETA: tomorrow)
- Rachel: author monitoring thresholds and dashboard tiles for Console (ETA: today)
- Alice: prepare Go + Python SDK snippets and a short testing checklist (ETA: EOD)

Support: I'll notify the affected customers and share the snippets. Also will propose per-tenant QPS caps during onboarding.

Mina: Thanks all. I'll push the one-pager to Confluence and cc the SE mailing list once it's ready.
